results.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Push-Up to Side Plank
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about knee height. Place your feet in the handles and assume a push-up position with your hands placed directly under your shoulders, arms fully extended, and body in a straight line from head to heels.
Perform a push-up by bending your elbows and lowering your chest towards the floor while keeping your body straight.
Push back up to the starting position and rotate your body to the right as you reach the top, extending your right arm towards the ceiling to enter a side plank position.
Return to the push-up position and repeat the movement, rotating to the left for the side plank. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the exercise on a non-slip surface to avoid slipping.
Focus on smooth transitions between the push-up and side plank for fluid motion.
Maintain even breathing to help keep your movements controlled and steady.
results.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Push-Up to Side Plank is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps, Upper Back.

results.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Reverse Push-Up
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles close to the floor. Grasp the handles with an underhand grip (palms facing forward) and position your body in a straight line, feet together and arms fully extended.
Engage your core and maintain a straight line from your head to your heels.
Lower your chest towards the handles by bending your elbows, keeping your body straight and elbows close to your sides.
Press through your hands to extend your arms and return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement with a steady and controlled tempo to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily: exhale as you push up and inhale as you lower your body.
Ensure your wrists are under your shoulders to maintain proper alignment.
results.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Reverse Push-Up is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Abdominals, Upper Back.

results.name: Svend Press Decline Bench
instructions: Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured under the foot pads and your back firmly against the bench. Hold a weight plate with both hands, pressing your palms against the flat sides of the plate at chest level with your fingers pointing up.
Engage your chest and press the weight plate straight out in front of you by extending your arms.
Squeeze your chest muscles as you press the plate outward until your arms are fully extended.
Slowly bring the plate back to your chest with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on pressing through your chest, not your shoulders, to emphasize chest muscle activation.
Choose a weight that challenges you but allows you to maintain proper form.
Avoid locking your elbows completely at the top of the movement to keep tension on the chest muscles.
results.description: Svend Press Decline Bench is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Band Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding the end of a resistance band, with your right hand, anchored under your right foot. Rest your forearm on your thigh with your palm facing up.
Start with your wrist extended down towards the floor, keeping your forearm stationary.
Curl your wrist upward, bringing your knuckles towards your forearm, squeezing your forearm muscles at the top of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position, extending your wrist downwards. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your forearm stationary on your thighs to isolate the wrist movement.
Focus on squeezing your forearm muscles at the top of the movement to enhance muscle activation.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you curl your wrists and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Band Wrist Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

results.name: Barbell Palm Down Wrist Curl Over a Bench
instructions: Kneel in front of a flat bench, holding a barbell with both hands, palms facing down (overhand grip). Rest your forearms on the bench with your wrists hanging over the edge and allow them to hang down.
Curl your wrists upward, lifting the barbell as high as possible while keeping your forearms flat on the bench.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid using your forearms or upper arms to lift the weight; the movement should come from your wrists.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid tensing them during the exercise.
Maintain a steady pace to ensure consistent tension in the muscles.
results.description: Barbell Palm Down Wrist Curl Over a Bench is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Forearms.

results.name: Cable Wrist Extension
instructions: Stand sideways, facing away from a low cable pulley and hold the handle with one hand using an underhand grip. Bend your elbow to approximately 90 degrees and keep it tucked against your side with your forearm stationary.
Extend your hand at the wrist joint, moving your hand downward while keeping the rest of your arm still. Pause for 1 - 2 seconds.
Curl the weight by flexing at the wrist joint, bringing your hand upward. Pause for 1 - 2 seconds.
Slowly lower your hand back to the starting position with control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.
tips: Keep your elbow tucked against your side throughout the exercise.
Move only at your wrist while keeping your forearm still.
Use a controlled range of motion without forcing your wrist beyond a comfortable position.
Inhale as you lower your hand and exhale as you raise it.
results.description: Cable Wrist Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Core.

results.name: Kettlebell Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit with your forearm resting on your thigh or a bench, palm up, holding a kettlebell by the handle.
Let your wrist bend back and lower the bell.
Curl your wrist up as far as possible.
Lower slowly and repeat, then switch hands.
tips: Only your wrist moves.
Use a light kettlebell.
results.description: Kettlebell Wrist Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category.

results.name: Kettlebell Wrist Extension
instructions: Sit with your forearm resting on your thigh or a bench, palm down, holding a kettlebell.
Let your wrist lower.
Raise the back of your hand as far as possible.
Lower slowly and repeat, then switch hands.
tips: Use a light weight.
Move only at the wrist.
results.description: Kettlebell Wrist Extension is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category.
